candidats.titre: File:2023-07-22 - Cirrocumulus lacunosus - solitary cloud - zenith - DSG1929-11 - crop mid right.jpg
candidats.description: A solitary Cirrocumulus lacunosus cloud nearing zenith (at top of image) is almost completely riddled with the namesake "hollows", typically arranged in a net or honeycomb pattern. This image, a crop of the full image, is aligned due west, the cloud overhead moving eastward. Image taken on 2023-07-22, 08:52 from the Aplerbecker Mark, Aplerbeck, Dortmund, Germany. This cloud formation is rather rare and is attributed to a cool layer of the atmosphere interacting with a warmer overlying layer.

candidats.description: This view is taken from a Mars Express flyover video of Flaugergues Crater on Mars. This image shows the beginning of the video, which begins by tracking along a swathe of ground enclosed by two steeply sloping and roughly parallel cliffs – or escarpments – named Scylla Scopulus and Charybdis Scopulus (to the left and right, respectively). A large crater named Bakhuysen Crater can be seen to the left. Flaugergues Crater itself can just about be seen to the keen eye, shrouded by haze in the distance.
